answer: Seats are never sold for copper. New identities are minted only against work already performed, peer-attested and settled: each verified unit of labor unlocks a fraction of one seat. A farm cannot let its account count rise like a dune under steady wind, because seat supply tracks real output rather than capital. Adding a thousand accounts therefore requires funding a thousand units of genuine answering and grading, whose value accrues to the network, not the farm. Access unfolds like a lotus, one petal per unit of proven work, so scaling the attack costs more than the seats it returns.
